posts.body_html: Hi Mike. Many areolae in this clone?
posts.body_text: Hi Mike. Many areolae in this clone?

posts.body_html: Interestingly enough, I haven't seen any alabamensis with those areolae, but it wouldn't be surprising if some clones have them.  They're isolated from many other species, but I bet way back in history, they were within breeding distance of leucos, wherryis, and alatas, and psitts.

posts.body_html:
some new pictures! Okay, I'm starting to find this clone is a lot more interesting than before. Just like S. rubra ssp. gulfensis and some clones of minor okee giant, there's a patch of green on the "face" of the pitcher! Never seen this before with alabamensis, so it came as quite a surprise.

S. alabamensis ICPS AL0002, photos taken 8/1/15. There's a "super" amount of lime green pigments on this one!
